stops.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
stops.why: Where Perseverance touched down on 18 Feb 2021. Flat, firm crater-floor rock: a proven safe landing and staging area.

photo.title: Mars Perseverance Sol 13: Left Navigation Camera (Navcam)
photo.caption: NASA's Mars Perseverance rover acquired this image using its onboard Left Navigation Camera (Navcam). The camera is located high on the rover's mast and aids in driving. This image was acquired on March 4, 2021 (Sol 13) at the local mean solar time of 14:29:25.

stops.name: Van Zyl Overlook
stops.why: Perseverance watched the Ingenuity helicopter's first flights from here. Open sightlines for communications and drone scouting.

stops.name: Roubion
stops.why: First coring attempt. The rock crumbled to powder, a warning that some crater-floor rocks are weak and weathered.

stops.name: Rochette (Citadelle ridge)
stops.why: First two rock cores (Montdenier, Montagnac). Volcanic rock altered by water, with salts that may hold ancient water bubbles.

photo.title: Mars Perseverance Sol 190: Left Navigation Camera (Navcam)
photo.caption: NASA's Mars Perseverance rover acquired this image using its onboard Left Navigation Camera (Navcam). The camera is located high on the rover's mast and aids in driving. This image was acquired on Sept. 1, 2021 (Sol 190) at the local mean solar time of 12:51:39.

stops.name: Brac (South Seitah)
stops.why: Olivine-rich igneous rock that reacted with water. Seitah's sand ripples make this a high-effort, high-value stop.

photo.title: Mars Perseverance Sol 262: Left Navigation Camera (Navcam)

stops.name: Issole (South Seitah)
stops.why: Cores Robine and Malay. Carbonate and sulfate minerals here record long-lived water.

photo.title: Mars Perseverance Sol 295: Left Navigation Camera (Navcam)
photo.caption: NASA's Mars Perseverance rover acquired this image using its onboard Left Navigation Camera (Navcam). The camera is located high on the rover's mast and aids in driving. This image was acquired on Dec. 18, 2021 (Sol 295) at the local mean solar time of 16:02:17.

stops.name: Skinner Ridge and Wildcat Ridge
stops.why: Delta-front sandstone and mudstone. Wildcat Ridge showed the mission's strongest organic-molecule signal: top target for signs of ancient life.

photo.title: Mars Perseverance Sol 490: Left Navigation Camera (Navcam)
photo.caption: NASA's Mars Perseverance rover acquired this image using its onboard Left Navigation Camera (Navcam). The camera is located high on the rover's mast and aids in driving. This image was acquired on July 7, 2022 (Sol 490) at the local mean solar time of 16:52:35.

stops.name: Amalik (Enchanted Lake)
stops.why: Fine-grained rock at the base of the delta, laid down in quiet lake water where biosignatures preserve best.

stops.name: Three Forks Sample Depot
stops.why: Ten sealed sample tubes were laid on the ground here as a backup cache for return to Earth. Flat and rock-free by design.
